(hereinafter referred to as the 'plaintiff') has filed a suit against the defendant 'M/s Yes Sir Catering Services Pvt. Ltd.' (hereinafter referred to as the 'defendant') through its Director for recovery of a sum of Rs.11,11,750.13 (Rupees Eleven Lakhs Eleven Thousand Seven Hundred Fifty and Thirteen Paise Only) alongwith pendente-lite C.S. sentences.text: 2. Brief facts of the case as revealed from the plaint are that the plaintiff is engaged in the business of supplying cooking masalas to the customers as per their orders.

Further, during the regular course of business, the defendant approached the plaintiff and placed orders with him to supply the cooking masalas to it from time to time and thereafter, the plaintiff started supplying the same to the defendant on 'Credit basis', vide various invoices, which were duly accepted and acknowledged by the defendant.
He also stated that the defendant also assured him that the bills would cleared periodically.

but the defendant kept on prolonging it on one pretext or the other and hence, the plaintiff sent it a legal notice dated 09.09.2020, vide which, he requested the defendant to pay him the outstanding amount of Rs.11,92,108.15/-, which included the principal amount as well as interest till the date of sending the legal notice, which also included other miscellaneous expenses.

He further submit that despite receiving the said notice, the defendant neither gave him C.S. (Comm.) 15/2021 Sh. Prehlad Rai Garg vs. M/s Yes Sir Catering Services Pvt. Ltd. page 2 of 26 any reply nor made the payment.

9. As per record, vide order dated 17.01.2022, following issues were framed by my Ld. Predecessor:-
i) Whether this Court does not have territorial C.S. (Comm.) 15/2021 Sh. Prehlad Rai Garg vs. M/s Yes Sir Catering Services Pvt. sentences.text:
12. In nutshell, the case of plaintiff is that though, he supplied the cooking masalas to the defendant as per orders placed by the defendant, however, the defendant did not pay him the entire amount,
for which he has filed the present case.

On the other hand, the defence of the defendant is that it never placed any such orders with the plaintiff to purchase cooking masalas and allege that its employee had placed the said orders with the plaintiff in connivance with the plaintiff and further allege that the plaintiff had supplied sub-standard masalas to it, due to which, the business and reputation of the defendant was adversely affected and hence, the defendant has no liability to make any payment to the plaintiff.
13.

Now, in the succeeding paragraphs, issues would be discussed and firstly, issue no.1 is discussed,
which is as under:-
Issue No. 1:-
"Whether this Court does not have territorial jurisdiction to entertain the present suit?"OPD
The onus to prove this issue is on the defendant.

14. From the perusal of record and from the testimonies C.S. (Comm.) 15/2021 Sh. Prehlad Rai Garg vs. M/s Yes Sir Catering Services Pvt. Ltd. page 6 of 26 of the witnesses examined by the parties, it is clearly shown on record that the transactions/business dealings between the parties pertaining to the present case also took place at Karawal Nagar, Delhi at the office of the plaintiff.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, PW-2, who is the son of the plaintiff and also used to do the business actively on behalf of the plaintiff has clearly stated during his cross examination that the plaintiff had shifted his business to Bawana, Delhi about two years back and prior to the same, the plaintiff was doing business from address at K-216, Mukund Vihar Road, Karawal Nagar, Delhi and he also stated that firstly, the business transaction between the parties took place on 17.07.2017.

It is pertinent to mention here that PW-2 stated so during his cross-examination as recorded on 10.03.2022 and as per plaintiff, the said transaction between the parties took place on 17.07.2017, at which point of time, the plaintiff was doing business from Karawal Nagar, Delhi.

The defendant could not show anything on record to the contrary and could not show if at the relevant time,
business transactions did not take place from the office of the plaintiff at Karawal Nagar, Delhi and the defendant could not shatter the version of PW-2 about the same.

Accordingly, in view of above, in considered opinion of the Court, the defendant could not show if this Court does not have the territorial jurisdiction to deal with the case, since, the area of Karawal Nagar, Delhi falls within territorial jurisdiction of this Court i.e. North-East District, C.S.
